findings.title: All-clients view permission bypasses client-specific denials
findings.body: canView(ClientModel) returns immediately when canView() grants the all-clients VIEW permission, without evaluating the target client's resource. Consequently, an administrator granted VIEW on all clients can still read a client with an explicit client-specific denying VIEW policy. The per-client evaluation must take precedence over the all-clients fallback, rather than treating the global fine-grained grant like an unconditional administrative role.

findings.title: Handle a missing Clients resource before evaluating the fallback
findings.body: The fallback assumes getResourceTypeResource() always returns a resource, but it can return null. In particular, a realm initialized with V2 permissions before this change has only the Users resource: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when the admin-permissions client already exists, so it never adds Clients or the new scopes. Checking a client in such a realm passes null to findByResource() and can subsequently dereference it at resource.getScopes(), producing a server error instead of an authorization decision. Reconcile existing schemas and guard the missing-resource case.
